subject: Request: carveout & attestation for short-term session logs
messages:

Cc: HelixMed Compliance <compliance@helixmed.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Short-term session logs — evidence + carveout ask

Hi Ben —

Quick one: our internal security team is prepping for a vendor audit (SIG + CAIQ) and flagged session-level ephemeral logs. Our baseline requirement for a subset of customers handling regulated PII is a 90-day accessible window for session metadata and replay traces for incident investigations.

We see Redwood defaults to 30d for ephemeral session logs in hosted mode; HelixMed needs either:
- a documented carveout/contract amendment guaranteeing 90-day hold for tenant X, or
- a compensating controls package + an attestation and extract procedure we can map to our audit.

Can you provide:
- the retention matrix for session and application logs (TTL by type and tier),
- a sample evidence extract/attestation we can include in our SIG submission, and
- an approximate timeline and cost impact to enable 90d for our tenant (if required)?

Attached: HelixMed-SIG-Questions.xlsx (first pass).

Thanks — appreciate a quick pointer to next steps.

—Maya
Maya Collins
Director, Security & Compliance | HelixMed
maya.collins@helixmed.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Collins <maya.collins@helixmed.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short-term session logs — evidence + carveout ask

Maya —

Thanks for the detail and the spreadsheet. Short answer: we can support both paths (contractual carveout or compensating controls). High-level options:

1) Contract amendment (90d tenant-scoped TTL)
   - Pros: straightforward for audit mapping; data retained in-place for 90d
   - Cons: incurs additional storage/retention fee and requires legal amendment

2) Forensics export + escrow/attestation workflow
   - Pros: no continuous cost for full 90d retention; we produce signed extracts on request or on a schedule
   - Cons: requires agreed SLAs for extract delivery (we typically do 72h for prioritized requests)

3) Targeted sampling + immutable audit trail
   - Keep 30d live, run a daily hashed index and retention proof that we keep for 90d; full payloads can be reconstituted for scoped investigations if retention policy allows

What I'll send you by EOD:
- our retention matrix CSV (TTL by log type & deployment) — attached (redwood-retention-matrix.csv)
- a draft attestation template you can include in your SIG packet
- example dataset extract (redacted) so you can validate schema (sample-session-logs-20260914.csv)

Next steps I propose: quick 30-min sync to pick path (amendment vs export). Grace/Rishi: can you confirm the extract format and estimated engineering lead time for a tenant-specific 90d TTL?

Best,
Ben Carter

Subject: Re: Short-term session logs — evidence + carveout ask

Hi all —

Technical notes from infra/security side:

- Default hosted TTL for ephemeral session traces is 30 days. Traces are stored in two tiers: hot KV (30d) + archival cold object store (configurable).
- For a tenant-scoped 90d live window we need to flip archival retention flags and pin the object store TTL; implementation is ~2–4 business days once legal signs off.
- For the export/attestation option we can provide:
  * daily S3-style export with SHA256 manifest per file (audit-extract-template.txt attached)
  * a signed attestation (PGP/PKI) that logs were archived per policy and deletion events are recorded in audit logs
- We will redact direct PII fields by default; if HelixMed requires raw payload delivery we need an LOA and additional controls.

Engineering impact/cost estimate:
- 90d pinned retention: +$0.015/GB-month (rough order) — final pricing after tenancy sizing
- Export-only path: no storage uplift, hourly work for scheduling and provisioning the extract endpoint (est. 1 week to automate)

I'll attach the internal audit extract template and a sample manifest. Ben — legal should get a short amendment draft for the 90d carveout.

Cheers,
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Product Manager, Security & Ops | Redwood Inference
From: Maya Collins <maya.collins@helixmed.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: HelixMed Compliance <compliance@helixmed.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 11:45:00 -0700

Ben / Grace —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our auditors:
- The SIG assessors accepted a compensating controls model if we get a signed attestation + automated daily manifest for 90 days.
- Our compliance team prefers the export be retained by Redwood for 90d (manifest + hashes) rather than HelixMed storing it; that reduces our operational burden.
- If you can supply a sample signed attestation (language our assessors expect) and the daily manifest format, we can tentatively close this in the SIG.

Can you expedite the attestation template? If possible we need it by EOD Fri so we can include it with our SIG round.

Onward —
Maya
